title: Simultaneous normalized immersion restrictions
statement: Fix a finite field datum and coefficient datum [def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex], and locally closed and open immersions h_0:W_0\hookrightarrow X_0 and j_0:U_0\hookrightarrow X_0 of separated finite-type schemes. There exist standard Frobenius comparison packages d_X,d_W,d_U and normalized natural local operators F_X,F_W,F_U of [def-zl-immersion-weil-local-data], and restriction packages R_h and R_j of that definition. The target data d_X and F_X are shared. Moreover the Frobenius comparison in R_j is the recorded zlFrobeniusSquare of [def-zl-weil-ind-sheaf-category]. This assertion contains no open extension operation.

source.place: Restriction paragraph and Part 2, extension-by-zero sentence

proof.text: Use the actual signed pullback shifts and their scalar descent. Apply the canonical t-exact comparison to Frobenius and each immersion. Lift the heart and canonical cohomology comparison to fixed pairs; identify the carrier equations by truncation uniqueness.

For each scheme define local operators from the three-factor localQbarClosedFrobenius on every coefficient cohomology degree. Naturality follows factor by factor. The finite-stage scalar normalization identifies them with localClosedFrobenius. Apply the residue-compatible theorem and immersion_residue to each map; its inverse-compositor and cohomology equations give every stalk clause. Use this same construction on the common target.

The integral normalization of zlPullComp agrees with the objectwise integral compositor defining the rational comparison, so scalar descent identifies the open pullback comparison with zlFrobeniusSquare, including all boundary equality maps.
